information_kinds.project_status: Routine progress, health, milestones, and high-level outcomes for the project.
information_kinds.timeline: Planned dates, deadlines, schedule changes, and delivery timing for the project.
information_kinds.blockers: Impediments, risks, dependencies, and open issues that affect project delivery.
information_kinds.operational_details: Day-to-day work, tasks, environments, processes, and non-sensitive implementation details.
information_kinds.budget_finance: Costs, spend, forecasts, invoices, and other confidential finance numbers tied to the project.
information_kinds.contract_terms: Contract scope, terms, obligations, and commercial commitments tied to the project.
information_kinds.customer_account: Customer-specific account details, requirements, and account context tied to the project.
information_kinds.hr_compensation: Staffing, performance, compensation, candidate feedback, and other HR matters tied to the project.
information_kinds.legal_strategy: Legal advice, litigation, compliance positions, and other legal strategy details.
information_kinds.security_findings: Vulnerabilities, security incidents, audit findings, and other security findings for the project.
information_kinds.credentials_secrets: Passwords, keys, tokens, certificates, and other secret material referenced in project discussions.
information_kinds.unreleased_strategy: Unreleased product roadmap, business strategy, go-to-market plans, and other unreleased strategy details.

role_reasons.contractor: Contractors are limited-scope participants, so they only need high-level routine status and schedule unless a scoped approval adds more.
role_reasons.employee: A generic employee working on a project needs routine status, schedule, blockers, and operational details to participate.
role_reasons.engineer: An engineer needs routine project context and operational details to build, test, and support the project.
role_reasons.executive: An executive needs high-level status, schedule, risks, and role-based need-to-know for finance and unreleased strategy.
role_reasons.executive_assistant: An executive assistant needs status, schedule, and blockers to coordinate the executive's project work without detailed operational access.
role_reasons.finance: A finance staff member needs routine project context and confidential finance numbers to manage project costs.
role_reasons.hr: An HR staff member needs routine project context and HR/compensation data to handle staffing and people matters.
role_reasons.legal: A legal staff member needs routine project context, legal strategy, and contract terms to provide legal guidance on the project.
role_reasons.manager: A manager needs routine project status, schedule, blockers, and operational details to coordinate delivery.
role_reasons.operations: An operations staff member needs routine project context and operational details to run and support the project.
role_reasons.procurement: A procurement staff member needs routine project context, finance numbers, and contract terms to manage purchasing and vendor costs.
role_reasons.product_manager: A product manager needs routine delivery details, customer account context, and unreleased strategy to define and track the project's product scope.
role_reasons.sales: A sales staff member needs routine status, schedule, blockers, customer account context, and contract terms to support customer-facing commitments.
role_reasons.security: A security staff member needs routine project context, operational details, and security findings to protect the project.
role_reasons.sre: An SRE needs routine project context, operational details, and security findings to maintain reliability and respond to issues.

authorities_reason: These roles have project ownership, senior sponsorship, or domain authority over the restricted information kinds stored about a project.
